Watcom shadow-pointer walk — `pCStack_2c` self-updates via the address of a constant index into itself plus a subfield path, where `N*sizeof(*pCStack_2c) + offsetof(subfield)` equals the real array stride. Replace `pCStack_2c->some_field[0]` (or the zero-index access) reads with direct indexing on the original pointer; drop the shadow init and self-update.

Watcom shadow-pointer walk — `pCStack_30` self-updates via the address of a constant index into itself plus a subfield path, where `N*sizeof(*pCStack_30) + offsetof(subfield)` equals the real array stride. Replace `pCStack_30->some_field[0]` (or the zero-index access) reads with direct indexing on the original pointer; drop the shadow init and self-update.

Watcom shadow-pointer walk — `pCStack_20` was initialized to the address of an array element's subfield (`pCStack_20 = &BASE->ARR[K].SUBFIELD;`) and is advanced here by `+ N` whole pointees, where `N * sizeof(*pCStack_20)` equals the array's element stride. The pointer is a smaller-typed walker striding a larger struct array. Replace the `pCStack_20->subfield` reads with direct indexing on the original array (`BASE->ARR[i].SUBFIELD`); drop the shadow init and advance.

Watcom shadow-pointer walk — `pCVar14` self-updates via pointer arithmetic on an inner array field reached through a chained field path; the array decays to a pointer and `+ CONST` adds `CONST * sizeof(element)` bytes, matching the outer array stride. Replace `pCVar14->some_field[0]` reads with direct indexing on the original pointer; drop the shadow init and self-update.
